tasks.title: Stored windows and optional file ids produce a stable effective maintenance set
tasks.spec: ## Repository: api, storage/file/effective-set portions of Behavior; D1, D6-D9; Checks 7 (array identity and service cache units), 8, 9 (projection lifecycle), 10 (view/export units, including the revised time boundary) and 11. Pin the merged contract main commit by full SHA and update the lockfile. Append migration 8 and implement the ordered transactional window store. Add optional unique file ids without changing legacy parsing, and preserve ids in validated snapshots. Implement the pure file-wins shadow split and projection, stripping identity from public windows and omitting missing effective check ids without rewriting definitions. The holder recomputes once on every setter, preserves its array between changes, and the service clears cached reads on a new array, including same-start note/end edits. Keep file windows first on ties and preserve all existing suppression behavior. Wire store loading into startup and snapshot fallback so seeded stored windows survive restart; preserve SQLite-before-holder publication. Strip file ids from the existing config view and export the effective flattened windows with ISO times; a seeded window at start 253402300799998 and end 253402300799999 must export the literal end '9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z' and pass the unchanged contract 66818a2 export validator. At this seam leave the existing admin write dispatch intact; switching maintenance HTTP writes belongs to T3, so existing route tests remain green. Exercise store CRUD/order/rollback through exported APIs in the listed tests, using seeded stored definitions where HTTP creation is not yet available. src/effective-maintenance.test.ts is new; the other test paths in this task already exist.

acceptance.expected: 0 fail; user_version 7 becomes 8 with 0 rows in maintenance_definitions; replace keeps creation order and rollback keeps stored definitions unchanged; snapshots with no window ids still load and snapshots with ids preserve them. A seeded database w for [a,b] is wholly shadowed by file id w, unshadowed on removal and restored after restart. Missing members stop projecting and apply again when the check returns. Two unchanged holder reads return the same array; each relevant setter publishes a new array. Focused coverage is not the acceptance gate.

acceptance.command: bun test src/config.maintenance.test.ts src/config.examples.test.ts src/service.maintenance.test.ts src/config-export.test.ts
acceptance.expected: 0 fail; existing file-window cases still pass; optional ids load, duplicate ids are refused and a 600-character file note loads. A new array with unchanged start and edited note/end changes the next cached read; deletion restores stored state. [1000,2000) excludes down at 1999 and counts down at 2000; file wins an equal-start tie. Public window keys are exactly checkId,start,end,note. Old config/export validators return ok:true for responses without ids; export flattens only effective windows in file-then-database order. Focused coverage is not the acceptance gate.

0 fail; a seeded database window with start 253402300799998 and end 253402300799999 exports end exactly '9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z', and the complete export returns literal ok:true from validateAdminConfigExport with the unchanged behavior of contract 66818a2. File windows precede projected database windows, exported entries have no id, and shadowed definitions are absent. Focused coverage is not the acceptance gate.

acceptance.command: bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun run test
acceptance.expected: exit 0; the full existing suite, including unchanged admin write dispatch, passes with at least 80% line coverage and the merged contract dependency.

tasks.title: Database maintenance writes share revisions, locking and atomic audit entries
tasks.spec: ## Repository: api, writer portion of Behavior; D2-D5 and D7; Checks 4 (writer revision and race units), 5 (writer validation/target rules), 6 (transactional audit), 7 (post-commit holder publication) and 10 (writer time-boundary validation). Implement the complete database writer as one transaction algorithm, using T1's store/holder and the existing ConfigWriteError, shared WriteLock, adminRevision and database generation. Validate the strict input with the merged contract and its MAX_MAINTENANCE_TIME = 253402300799999; check all effective references before target/cap conflicts, retain creation order, compute phase from injected now at read/response time, and support the exact file-only, shadowed and legacy decimal-index target rules of D4. Accept start 253402300799998/end 253402300799999; refuse both create and replace with end 253402300800000 or 8640000000000000 without changing stored definitions. Definition, generation and maintenance.create/replace/delete audit commit together; update the holder only after success. A stale revision changes neither definitions, generation, audit nor holder. No writer dependency may read, test writability of or write the checks file; invalid, unreadable, read-only and written-not-applied file states do not block a fresh database write. Audit/error text holds no note. This task creates src/maintenance-write.test.ts and supplies and tests the writer before HTTP/startup dispatch is changed in T3.

acceptance.expected: 0 fail; all D2 writer counterexamples use invalid errors, including []/51/duplicate/missing check ids, invalid time bounds and invalid note/id text. 50 ids and note lengths 1/500 succeed; UTF-16 lengths 500/502 accept/refuse as specified. The 1000th create succeeds and the 1001st conflicts. Duplicate/file-only ids and shadowed replace conflict; shadowed delete succeeds and preserves the file; legacy in-range decimal delete conflicts and out-of-range returns not-found. Phase at start-1/start/end is planned/current/past. Focused coverage is not the acceptance gate.

0 fail; tests named with 'time boundary' prove create and replace accept start 253402300799998/end 253402300799999 and reject end 253402300800000 and end 8640000000000000 with ConfigWriteError code invalid. Rejected writes change neither the stored list, database generation, audit count nor effective set. Focused coverage is not the acceptance gate.

0 fail; old revisions after a check write, file apply or window write give stale, including a check write after a window write. Two writes with one revision yield exactly 1 success and 1 stale. Each successful window edit adds exactly 1 audit entry with maintenance.create/replace/delete, target {kind:'maintenance',id:'w'}, actor and resulting revision; injected audit failure leaves definition/list, generation, audit count and effective set unchanged. Database writes leave file bytes/state/lastAppliedAt unchanged for all D5 file states. Focused coverage is not the acceptance gate.

acceptance.command: bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun run test
acceptance.expected: exit 0; the new writer and the existing check/component/file protocols pass the full suite and the 80% line coverage gate.

tasks.title: Admin maintenance routes store database windows and expose the effective set end to end
tasks.spec: ## Repository: api, remaining HTTP/startup Behavior, all Docs, Checks 1-6 and 7/9/10 at HTTP boundaries (including the revised Check 10 timestamp/export boundary), Check 12, and Completion evidence; D1-D9; Security impact and Performance impact. Wire T2's writer with the same db/audit/holder/writeLock as checks, fileRevision from reloader.revision and injected now; add databaseMaintenanceWindows to the listening log. GET /admin/maintenance lists effective and shadowed windows, including all phases, with the shared revision, ETag and no-store. POST/PUT/DELETE dispatch exclusively to the database writer, bypass assertWritable, use client ids for Location and logs, enforce body/path identity and the exact D4 permission/status/method/query/body-limit rules. Stop handing window edits to the file writer while keeping component writes, their 503 behavior and legacy audit_pending resolution unchanged. Update existing file-write route expectations in the same task. src/metrics.ts is conditional: maintenance is already a supported write kind, so reuse its existing vocabulary unless the section requires a change. Create src/server.maintenance-admin.test.ts for real-server HTTP regressions for all numbered checks and every Counterexamples row, including down quorum/heartbeat suppression, complete shadowing/reappearance/restart, broken-file writes, cross-resource stale revisions and concurrent writes, audit rollback, immediate note/end/delete visibility, missing-member removal/recreation and strict old-console views/exports. Check 10 creates start 253402300799998/end 253402300799999 with 201, asserts the literal exported end '9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z' and ok:true from the old contract export validator, and checks both POST and PUT reject end 253402300800000 or 8640000000000000 with 422 and no list change. Preserve baseline-compatible HTTP versions of Checks 1-4 and show their behavioral assertions failing on 32704fd1e2217a109f51ea7ff41ccc7e8c73cfeb, not merely an import/type failure, before implementing routes. Fix the concepts reload contradiction, document both sources, optional file ids, read-only file entries, new routes, status order, reference lifecycle and identity loss on export; retain component statements. Complete every applicable Security impact item with test evidence and record the checklist, no new runtime dependency, full merged contract pin, four red/green assertions, required checks, manual bun start commands/responses and before/after performance numbers in the PR. API ships no Compose end-to-end stack (src/compose-moved.test.ts); use its real HTTP tests and the manual startup exercise. If Docker is available run the spec's bench/run.ts A/B command; otherwise measure full-suite CPU on baseline and branch with /usr/bin/time as the spec directs.

acceptance.command: bun test src/server.maintenance-admin.test.ts src/config-admin.test.ts src/start.file-fallback.test.ts src/config-export.test.ts
acceptance.expected: 0 fail; Checks 1-4 fail behaviorally on baseline 32704fd and pass on the branch, with the assertion of each recorded in the PR. POST w for [a,b] is 201 with Location /admin/maintenance/w and a new ETag; exactly 2 public entries have only checkId,start,end,note, a/b show maintenance with note 'db upgrade', b has 0 incidents and consecutiveDown 0, while c opens 1 incident; heartbeats in the window do not expire. File id w reports source:file/index:0/note:'file note', shadows the whole stored [a,b], and only the stored copy can be deleted. Broken-file POST/PUT/DELETE are 201/200/204 with identical file bytes/state/lastAppliedAt and survive snapshot restart; EROFS never produces 503 for window writes. Stale window/check revisions return 412 with no mutation; two concurrent POSTs give exactly one 201 and one 412. Cache edits are visible on the next GET; references disappear/reappear without changing stored checkIds; old config/export validators return ok:true. Focused coverage is not the acceptance gate.

0 fail; tests named with 'time boundary' POST {id:'w',checkIds:['a'],start:253402300799998,end:253402300799999,note:'x'} using a fresh revision and receive 201. GET /admin/config/export includes end exactly '9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z'; validateAdminConfigExport of contract 66818a24b81f5d0d86eee939dad64fa126617ba2 returns literal ok:true for the complete response. Use that independent old validator, without a new runtime dependency; T1 also pins the merged contract whose export behavior remains unchanged. With fresh revisions, POST and PUT with end 253402300800000 or 8640000000000000 each return 422 and leave the list unchanged. Focused coverage is not the acceptance gate.

0 fail; D4 status order and all Counterexamples are asserted literally: feature off 404, missing credential 401, probe/admin-only/checks-only writes 403, read-token GET 200 and write 403, 1048577-byte bodies 413 on GET/DELETE as well as writes, bad JSON/If-Match/path mismatch 400, missing If-Match 428, stale 412 before schema/conflict checks, invalid schema/reference 422, conflict 409 and unknown id 404. Collection Allow is GET, POST; item Allow is PUT, DELETE; unsupported methods are 405; GET query parameters are 400. Legacy POST/PUT/DELETE answer 422/400/409 (or 404 for an absent index) without file edits. Every successful write adds exactly 1 correct audit entry; audit failure is 500 with no mutation. Notes appear 0 times in captured errors/logs/audit. The applicable Security impact checklist is covered; component writes on EROFS retain 503. Focused coverage is not the acceptance gate.
